B1:
Cause: Touched fires many times, once per body part that touches and repeatedly while contact jitters. Several events are already queued before Destroy runs. With deferred signals they all run, and each one adds 10.
Fix: debounce with a "collected" flag that is set before granting anything, and validate the Humanoid.
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if collected then return end
  local char = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local plr = char and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(char)
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not plr or not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  collected = true
  local coins = plr:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") and plr.leaderstats:FindFirstChild("Coins")
  if coins then coins.Value += 10 end
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning pickups, use per-player cooldowns instead of Destroy. Run this in a server Script.
B2:
Diagnosis: with StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player, inside StreamingTargetRadius. Distant parts of the map are not replicated yet, or have been streamed out (parented to nil), so indexing workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel.Door with dot syntax errors when the script starts. That is why it happens mostly far from spawn. A model may also arrive in pieces, since ModelStreamingMode defaults to Nonatomic.
Fix 1: tags. Tag doors with CollectionService ("Door"). Handle GetTagged plus GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door") to connect Touched, and GetInstanceRemovedSignal to clean up. This works for doors that stream in later and is the recommended pattern.
Fix 2: wait for the model. Set the Door/Hotel model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (or Persistent if it must always exist), then use WaitForChild for each level with a timeout, and handle nil and re-streaming:
```lua
local door = workspace:WaitForChild("Map"):WaitForChild("Buildings")
  :WaitForChild("Hotel", 10)
door = door and door:WaitForChild("Door", 10)
```
Alternative: do the touch logic on the server, which has everything loaded.
B3:
Bugs:
1. Always returns PurchaseGranted, even when pcall failed. The player is charged and gets nothing.
2. The pcall result is ignored.
3. No idempotency. Retried receipts or a crash after the save grant the coins again (double coins). PurchaseId is never recorded.
4. GetAsync followed by SetAsync is not atomic, so concurrent writes race and lose or double values. Use UpdateAsync.
5. plr can be nil if the player left; plr.UserId then errors and the callback fails. Use info.PlayerId.
6. No ProductId check, so every product grants 100.
7. Live session data and the DataStore can diverge.
Correct behaviour:
- Look up the player. If they are not in the server or their data is not loaded, return NotProcessedYet.
- In one UpdateAsync on the player's key: if info.PurchaseId is already in data.Receipts, change nothing. Otherwise add coins for that ProductId and store the PurchaseId (cap the list).
- If the pcall fails, return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries.
- Only after a successful save, return PurchaseGranted, and update leaderstats or session data.
- Have one ProcessReceipt and never throw.
B4:
Metatables are stripped. Remote arguments are serialized to plain data, and functions and metatables don't replicate. The client receives {Name="Rifle", Ammo=30} without the Weapon metatable, so w.Fire is nil and w:Fire() fails with 'attempt to call a nil value'. Mixed or non-string keys and cyclic tables are also lost or mangled.
The client can't see ServerStorage. Instances pass as references only if the receiving side has them replicated. ServerStorage never replicates, so the Muzzle argument arrives as nil. The same happens for a part that hasn't streamed in.
Fix:
- Send plain data and rebuild the object on the client: put the Weapon class in a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage and call `local w = Weapon.new(data)` (setmetatable on receive).
- Put shared assets in ReplicatedStorage, or clone the part into Workspace or ReplicatedStorage before sending it. Or send an identifier (a name or id) and let the client look it up or clone it from ReplicatedStorage.
- Keep the authoritative state on the server.
B5:
What's wrong: the second argument of workspace:Raycast is the direction vector, and its length is the ray's range. .Unit has length 1, so the ray is only 1 stud long and only hits things touching the barrel. The shooter's own character can also block the ray.
Fix:
```lua
local MAX = 500
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * MAX   -- or (target - origin) for exactly to target
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
Also guard against origin == target, where .Unit gives NaN. Do the authoritative raycast on the server and validate the client's target.
B6:
Cause: when the last player leaves, the server starts shutting down right away. PlayerRemoving handlers that yield (SetAsync is an async web call) may not finish, because the process closes before the request completes, so the save is lost. The same happens when the server shuts down for updates.
Standard fix: game:BindToClose. In it, save every remaining player's data in parallel (task.spawn per player) and wait until all saves finish or about 25 s pass. Roblox gives about 30 s total. Make the PlayerRemoving and BindToClose saves share one save function with a per-player "saving/saved" guard so the data isn't written twice. Use UpdateAsync with pcall and retries instead of a blind SetAsync, and release the session lock. Add periodic autosave (every 60-120 s, staggered) so a crash loses little. In Studio, skip or shorten the BindToClose wait (RunService:IsStudio()) if you need to.
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse = {} -- [Player] = time

local function doAbility(player, abilityId) --[[ server effect ]] end

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
  if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" or #abilityId > 32 then return end
  local now = os.clock()
  local last = lastUse[player]
  if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  lastUse[player] = now      -- set before any yield
  doAbility(player, abilityId)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
  lastUse[player] = nil      -- no leak
end)
```
The cooldown is authoritative on the server and the client's timer is cosmetic only. os.clock() is monotonic. The table is keyed by Player and cleared on leave; you could also use a weak-keyed table.
B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local GEMS100 = 123456
local handlers = {
  [GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end,
}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
  if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- left: retry later

  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    store:UpdateAsync("u_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
      data = data or {Gems = 0, Receipts = {}}
      data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
      if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
      handler(data)
      data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
      -- (prune old receipts to bound size)
      return data
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then
    warn("Receipt failed:", err)
    return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
  end
  -- sync session/leaderstats here (e.g. reload or add to cached profile)
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Return PurchaseGranted only after the durable write succeeds. The function is idempotent per PurchaseId, never errors, and is set only once on the server. If you use a session-locked profile, write into it and save instead of a direct UpdateAsync.
B9:
```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN  = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = HIDDEN
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = SHOWN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = HIDDEN})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```
Visible becomes false only when the slide-out completes, and not if it was interrupted by a reopen. menu.AnchorPoint should be (0.5, 0.5).

```lua
local RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end

  end
```

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns = {} -- [part] = connection

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local model = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then

    end
  end)

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then
    c:Disconnect()
    conns[part] = nil
  end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do

end
```

B13:
(a) Buying: a client-to-server RemoteFunction (InvokeServer returns the result) or a RemoteEvent. The client sends only the intent, buy "Sword". The server validates the item (exists, price from a server catalog, sufficient coins, rate limit), deducts and grants, and returns success or a reason.
(b) Updating the counter: server-to-client. Best is a leaderstats IntValue or a player attribute/Value that replicates automatically, which the UI listens to with .Changed or GetAttributeChangedSignal. Otherwise use a RemoteEvent with FireClient.
Where things live: the balance and all validation stay on the server in session data, saved to a DataStore. The client is display only and is never trusted for price or balance.
Why not server InvokeClient: the server would yield waiting on the client. An exploiter or disconnected client can hang it forever (it never returns), error it, or return garbage, which can stall or break server code. The client being gone also errors. One-way server-to-client should be a RemoteEvent or replicated state; there is no need for a reply.
B14:
Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData or GetJoinData().TeleportData) travels through the client. It is visible to and editable by exploiters, has a size limit, and is lost if the teleport fails or the player rejoins differently. It is fine only for non-authoritative hints: the chosen map, party or match id, cosmetic loadout preference that you re-validate.
DataStores are authoritative and persistent, but they need a save in the lobby and a load in the match (latency), plus a session lock so the lobby's final save lands before the match loads. Otherwise stale reads and dupes happen.
MemoryStores (SortedMap/HashMap) are fast, cross-server and expire (TTL). They are good for transient match-assignment state or a handoff of the loadout, but they are not durable.
Choice: keep coins in the DataStore-backed profile with session locking (UpdateAsync/ProfileStore). Save and release the lock before TeleportAsync, then load with lock-acquire retries in the match place. Validate the loadout against owned items on the server; it can be sent as teleport data or a MemoryStore entry for speed, but re-check it. Never trust the coin balance from teleport data.
B15:
Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): every copy runs its own thread and connections, so there is more memory and scheduler overhead. Fixing a bug means editing hundreds of copies, which drift apart. Clones duplicate code, and copies don't handle instances spawned or streamed later unless they're cloned with the script. It is hard to profile or disable globally.
Tag-driven architecture: tag instances with CollectionService ("Door", "Pickup", "Turret"). One server Script or module system per type requires a ModuleScript and binds behaviour:
- `for _, x in CS:GetTagged(tag) do setup(x) end` plus `CS:GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag):Connect(setup)` for spawned or streamed-in instances.
- `CS:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag):Connect(cleanup)` disconnects connections and clears state tables, so nothing leaks.
- Configuration goes in attributes on each instance (OpenTime, Damage, Respawn).
- Turrets use a single central Heartbeat loop iterating a set rather than 60 loops, staggered or throttled, possibly with Parallel Luau.
- On the client (StreamingEnabled), visuals and prompts use the same tag signals, because instances stream in and out. The server stays authoritative.
The result is one place for logic, consistent behaviour, and easy hot-fixes.
B16:
Ownership: give the driver network ownership of the car's assembly, VehicleSeat:SetNetworkOwner(driverPlayer) when they sit and back to nil (server) or auto when they leave. Client physics gives responsive, lag-free driving; server-owned cars feel laggy. Unoccupied cars stay server-owned.
Security risk: the owning client simulates the car's physics, and the server accepts its positions. An exploiter can teleport the car, speed-hack, fly, noclip, fling other players, or move it to checkpoints and the finish line.
What the server must still validate:
- Speed and position sanity: max velocity and acceleration per tick, and teleport distance. Snap back or reclaim ownership (SetNetworkOwner(nil)) on violation.
- Checkpoints passed in order, minimum lap time, and the finish line through server-side detection (region or zone checks on server positions, not client-reported touches).
- Who can drive (occupant matches the owner) and seat changes.
- Collisions or damage to others, rewards and the leaderboard, all computed on the server.
- Rate-limit any remotes such as boost or nitro, and check cooldowns and resources on the server.
Under the new Server Authority mode, the server simulates with client prediction instead.
B17:
Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent (or send at a lower rate) for continuous aim and position data. Only the latest value matters, so dropped or late packets are fine.
Constraints and how to handle them:
- Delivery is best-effort, unordered and may drop. Include a sequence number or timestamp and ignore stale packets. Interpolate on the receiver.
- Payloads over about 1,000 bytes are dropped. Send a few compact numbers, for example yaw/pitch as int16 in a buffer, or quantized Vector3s, instead of tables or CFrames.
- There is a rate throttle (about 500/s per client, shared across remotes of that type). Excess is dropped, not queued, and messages with no connected handler are discarded.
- Never send must-arrive events (fire, hit, purchase, state change) on it. Those use a reliable RemoteEvent.
Also: lower the rate to 10-20 Hz and send only when the value changes by more than a threshold. Batch per frame. Character position already replicates through physics, so don't resend it. The server must still validate and rate-limit aim data, because it is client-supplied.
B18:
Approach: put each NPC (or batch of NPCs) under an Actor, with the AI script parented to the Actor. Each Heartbeat, the scripts call task.desynchronize() (or use ConnectParallel), then do the read-only work in parallel: workspace:Raycast with per-NPC RaycastParams, path or target scoring, distance math. Write the results into local tables, then call task.synchronize() and apply the effects serially: MoveTo, Humanoid changes, damage, property writes, firing remotes. Spread NPCs over about 8-16 Actors so the engine schedules them across cores. Also stagger: not every NPC needs to think every frame (10 Hz, round-robin), and cache paths.
Limitations to design around:
- In the parallel phase you can read the DataModel and raycast, but you cannot write most properties, create or destroy instances, or call many yielding or unsafe APIs. Defer those to the serial phase.
- Actors don't share Lua state. Communicate through SharedTable, Actor messages (SendMessage/BindToMessage) or attributes.
- Every sync/desync switch has a cost, so batch the work.
- PathfindingService ComputeAsync isn't parallel-safe; compute paths serially and less often.
- Results lag by one frame, and work must be deterministic per Actor. Profile with the MicroProfiler to confirm the speedup.
B19:
Change: set Workspace.StreamingEnabled = true in Studio's Properties panel (it can't be set by script).
Sensible settings:
- StreamingMinRadius: default 64. Always kept loaded. Raise it, for example to 128-256, for fast travel or vehicles.
- StreamingTargetRadius: default 1024, and it must be larger than the min. Lower it, for example to 512-768, for mobile memory.
- StreamingIntegrityMode: PauseOutsideLoadedArea, recommended, or MinimumRadiusPause.
- ModelStreamingMode on Models: Nonatomic is the default. Use Atomic for interactables that must arrive whole (doors, NPCs, vehicles). Use Persistent sparingly (always loaded, for example landmarks). Use PersistentPerPlayer with Model:AddPersistentPlayer.
- Model LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for distant imposters. Optionally use Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleports.
Scripts that assumed everything is loaded:
- Replace dot-path indexing of Workspace parts in LocalScripts with WaitForChild (with a timeout) on Atomic models.
- Better, use CollectionService tags with GetInstanceAddedSignal and GetInstanceRemovedSignal to set up and clean up as instances stream in and out.
- Don't cache workspace references forever; parts are parented to nil when streamed out.
- Keep client-needed data in ReplicatedStorage, attributes or remotes.
Server scripts are unaffected because the server has everything.
B20:
Cause: 80 players saving every 5 s is about 960 SetAsync calls per minute, all bunched on the same tick. Each DataStore request type has a request queue of 30. Burst writes overflow it and requests fail (301-306, e.g. 302 queue full), while queued saves take seconds to tens of seconds. Writing the same key faster than the per-key limits (historically about once per 6 s) also throttles. Failed or dropped SetAsync calls, with no retry, lose data, and blind SetAsync can overwrite newer data. The experience-wide budget (300 + 20 x CCU writes/min = 1,900) is not the problem; the bursty pattern is.
Better design:
- Keep data in memory (session cache) and autosave every 60-180 s, staggered per player with random jitter.
- Save only dirty profiles.
- Use UpdateAsync with a session lock, not SetAsync.
- Save on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose (in parallel, within about 25 s).
- Wrap every call in pcall with exponential-backoff retries, and check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before background writes.
- Or use ProfileStore/ProfileService, which implements all of this.

B22:
The Input Action System is a declarative, instance-based input API that replaces UserInputService and ContextActionService bindings. It works across keyboard, gamepad and touch, and its instances exist on both client and server.
Three core instances:
1. InputContext: a group of actions with Enabled, Priority and Sink.
2. InputAction: one action, with Type Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D, Direction3D or ViewportPosition.
3. InputBinding: maps hardware to the action, using KeyCode (keys or gamepad buttons), modifiers, UIButton (an on-screen GuiButton for touch), thresholds and Scale/vector composites.
How an action signals a press: for Bool actions, InputAction.Pressed and InputAction.Released fire. StateChanged(newState) fires for any type, and GetState() polls the current value; poll it for held analog input. Fire() drives the action from code.
Menu precedence: put menu actions in their own InputContext with a higher Priority than the gameplay or default player-script contexts, and set Sink = true so the inputs it binds are consumed and don't reach lower contexts. Enable it while the menu is open and disable it when closed. The default player scripts use IAS when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is Enabled.
B23:
The CSS-like system is Roblox's engine UI styling: "Styles" with a beta Style Editor.
Main instances:
- StyleSheet: a container of rules, and of tokens as attributes.
- StyleRule: a Selector string plus property values (SetProperty/SetProperties). Rules can nest.
- StyleLink: attaches a StyleSheet to a UI tree, for example a ScreenGui (StyleLink.StyleSheet = sheet). There is one sheet per tree.
- StyleDerive: lets a sheet inherit or extend another sheet, for example base tokens plus a theme.
- StyleQuery: conditional or responsive rules, such as MaxSize or PreferredInput.
How styles reach the UI: the StyleLink under a ScreenGui or LayerCollector applies its sheet to that tree. Each StyleRule's Selector matches GuiObjects by class (TextButton), by tag (CollectionService tags, ".Primary"), by name ("#Close"), and by pseudo state or modifiers (GuiState such as hover or press, "::UICorner" child modifiers). Matched properties are applied, with specificity and order resolving conflicts, much like CSS.
Tokens: define a value once as an attribute on a token StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor = Color3), and reference it in rules as "$PrimaryColor". Swap themes by switching a StyleDerive between token sheets that use the same names, and every rule using the token updates.
Gotcha: don't also set the same property from scripts, because they will fight.
B24:
Method: an age check, usually Facial Age Estimation in the Roblox app through a vendor (Persona). ID verification can be used instead, and parents can correct the age through Parental Controls. Without a check, chat is unavailable.
Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, and 21+.
Restriction: by default a user can chat only with their own age group and the groups directly next to it (one above and one below). For example, 9-12 can chat with under 9, 9-12 and 13-15. This blocks minors and adults from chatting freely; under-16s can't chat with adults. Trusted Connections (13+, people known in real life, verified) can widen contact. Under-9s have chat off unless a parent consents.
Players who can't talk to each other simply don't see each other's messages, with no indicator, and no API exposes a player's age group.
Rollout: select regions (e.g. Australia, New Zealand, Netherlands) in Dec 2025, then worldwide in early Jan 2026.
Design implication: don't make gameplay depend on chat. Use pings, emotes, quick chat, and TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage for system text.
